transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-26
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (ZephyrSearch Head of Search), Ethan Park (CTO), Dana Li (ML Engineer)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + rerank endpoints for improving search relevance. Covered architecture, sample integration (curl + SDK), latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a POC and benchmark. Customer wants to validate quality vs their current Elastic-based pipeline and understand VPC/data residency and SOC2 posture.

Topics:
- Embeddings API / index flow
- Rerank endpoint and scoring integration
- Latency vs cost; batching / KV cache options
- Hosted vs Dedicated / Private (VPC) tradeoffs
- Security / compliance (SOC2, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Maya (ZephyrSearch): Good thanks, excited to see how you handle reranking, we've been fighting with our current relevance.
[00:10] Liam (Redwood SE): Cool, we'll start with a quick overview then jump into a live demo of embeddings + rerank. I'll show a small index and run a few queries.
[00:18] Ethan (CTO): One thing up front — we care about both throughput and reproducible relevance. Our traffic is bursty from 9-11am and 4-6pm.
[00:25] Dana (ML Eng): And we have a dataset of ~8 million docs, avg doc length 400 tokens, queries ~6 tokens.
[00:31] Sofia: Perfect, that helps. Liam, do you want to show the architecture slide?
[00:34] Liam: Sure — (screen) so the hosted flow we demo is: user query -> embeddings endpoint -> vector store + ANN -> candidate retrieval -> rerank endpoint which uses the original query + candidate documents as context to produce final scores. We have automatic prefix caching and KV cache for autoregressive models but for rerank we usually run short-context models so KV isn't heavy.
[00:52] (murmur)
[00:55] Maya: When you say "rerank endpoint" what exactly is the input/response shape, is it just scores or a re-ordered list?
[01:01] Liam: Good question. Our rerank endpoint returns a score and optionally a re-ranked list; you can configure it to return just top-k ids or full snippets. Example: POST /v1/rerank with payload {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":1,"text":"..."},...]} -> response includes scores, and we provide a 'explain' toggle for reasons.
[01:20] Dana: Is the explain deterministic? We need to audit regressions.
[01:23] Liam: Explain is heuristic but reproducible per model/version. If you pin model versions in the API call you get stable outputs; we also log model version and seed in request metadata.
[01:32] Ethan: What about latency? Our SLO is 120ms P95 for search.
[01:36] Liam: For embeddings + ANN retrieval we commonly hit <50ms P95 for vector lookup with our recommended ANN config; reranker depends on model size — small cross-encoders can be ~40-80ms. For strict 120ms P95 you might use a smaller reranker or a two-stage approach: cheap lexical + embeddings retrieval, then rerank only top-10.
[01:53] Maya: Sounds like what we do now, but our current reranker is CPU-based and slow.
[01:58] Sofia: We can run a benchmark against your queries; Liam has a template.
[02:02] Liam: I'll show a quick demo — loading a sample dataset into a temporary vector index. (screen) I'm using our hosted embeddings endpoint here — note the curl sample in the docs: https://redwood.example/docs/embeddings (note: example link).
[02:15] [02:15] Speaker 2: (typing sounds)
[02:18] Liam: Ok curl to /v1/embeddings with API key -> we get the vector back. Then we insert into an ANN store (we demo using the hosted index). Now I'll run a candidate retrieval for the query "status update on shipment" — we get 10 candidates.
[02:34] Maya: Are you using HNSW under the hood?
[02:36] Liam: Yes, HNSW is the default; we also support IVF/OPQ for large corpora — we tune based on recall/latency tradeoff.
[02:44] Dana: Are those index configs exposed in console?
[02:47] Liam: Yup, Console shows per-index settings, recall targets, and we provide recommendations via the Optimize tab — it'll say "increase ef_search" or suggest quantization profiles for reduced cost.
[02:58] (brief pause)
[03:02] Liam: Now rerank — sending POST /v1/rerank with the 10 candidates; model is a cross-encoder 3B quantized. Response comes back ~62ms in this demo. Scores and a short 'why' snippet.
[03:14] Maya: That 62ms includes network time to hosted?
[03:18] Liam: Yes this is hosted in us-west region; your latency will vary by region. For strict low-latency needs we recommend Dedicated capacity in the same region or Private if you want VPC and pinned hardware.
[03:29] Ethan: Can you clarify Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs — cost and isolation?
[03:33] Sofia: Hosted is usage-based, easiest to get started; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools (monthly commit) for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private gives you VPC and on-prem options with compliance controls. We can share a chart.
[03:45] Ethan: And data at rest encryption? KMS?
[03:47] Sofia: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private and Dedicated, and managed keys for Hosted. We'll share SOC2 doc.
[03:54] (mumble)
[03:58] Maya: For our POC, we care about cost per query — do you have ballpark numbers?
[04:02] Sofia: Ballpark depends on model choice and batching. For embeddings + rerank using a small cross-encoder on hosted you're usually in X-1 cents per query on our baseline sample; we'll give you explicit numbers after we see your query volume and model selection.
[04:16] Dana: Can you run against our dataset? We can share a 100k sample.
[04:19] Sofia: Yes please share the sample. Liam will run the benchmark and we'll return a detailed report.
[04:24] Liam: Quick note on common mis-hearings — the KV cache I mention is K V cache for autoregressive gen models, not relevant to rerank but useful if you use generation-based reranking.
[04:35] (laugh)
[04:38] Liam: Now switching to Console to show the Optimize tab — here we have cost breakdown per-token, per-request, and per-route. You can see suggestions: reduce model to 1.5B or enable 4-bit quantization for rerank to save 35% at a small accuracy delta.
[04:56] Maya: How do you detect accuracy regressions?
[05:00] Liam: We have eval harnesses. You can upload labeled queries and we run A/B with rollout policies. We surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:08] Ethan: Any limits on uploading customer data?
[05:11] Sofia: We support Data Residency controls; for Hosted we have region options and retention settings. For enterprise-level rules you can use Private.
[05:20] Maya: What about integration effort? We currently do a pipeline with Elastic + a custom ranker.
[05:24] Liam: Integration is straightforward — embeddings API calls, index push (or use your existing vector DB), then rerank with the candidate payload. We have SDKs (Python/JS) with examples. Typical engineering effort for a POC is 1-2 weeks.
[05:36] Dana: Do you support streaming or batch rerank?
[05:39] Liam: Rerank is request/response; for batch offline scoring you can call the rerank endpoint in bulk. For high throughput we recommend batching candidates per request and using our bulk endpoints.
[05:50] Maya: Any concerns about reproducibility when you update models?
[05:53] Sofia: You can pin model versions per-route, and Console shows model change history. Rollouts are supported (canary/A-B) so you can test before full rollout.
[06:03] Ethan: Competitors — we evaluate Pinecone + OpenAI right now; how are you different?
[06:07] Sofia: Pinecone is an index provider — Redwood is a full inference platform plus routing, rerank, and cost controls. OpenAI provides models but not the same hosting/routing for private deployments. Weave... Weaviate is similar to Pinecone in vector ops.
[06:21] (notes)
[06:25] Liam: I'll paste a sample rerank curl in chat now: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":...,"text":"..."}]}' (example, see docs).
[06:38] Maya: Great — could you also show quantization impact?
[06:40] Liam: Quick sim: same model quantized 4-bit, inference latency down 30% and cost down ~40% with small drop in nDCG (~0.01). Optimize suggests these changes per-route.
[06:52] Dana: For the POC, we'll want the code snippet plus an example scoring script.
[06:56] Liam: I'll attach that to the benchmark ticket.
[07:00] Sofia: Ok to recap next steps — Dana will share the 100k sample and traffic profile, Liam will run a 10k/100k benchmark using our template, Sofia will send pricing and SOC2, and we'll target a POC kickoff week of Aug 6.
[07:15] Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[07:18] Ethan: We'll need legal to review terms if we go Dedicated/Private — that's fine.
[07:22] Sofia: We'll include a procurement checklist.
[07:25] (wraps up)
[07:28] Sophia (sic, quick mislabel): Thanks everyone, speak soon.
[07:32] (recording ends)
